title: Quantum Entangled Multimodal Fusion Networks (QEMFN): Resource-Aware Hybrid Vision-Language Fusion via Trainable Entanglement
authors: Srikar Alla, Ali Shiri Sichani, Chi-Ren Shyu
abstract: Multimodal vision-language systems typically fuse image and text embeddings through classical operators such as concatenation, attention, bilinear pooling, or tensor interactions. We propose Quantum Entangled Multimodal Fusion Networks (QEMFN), a hybrid quantum-classical framework that introduces parameterized entanglement as a structured inductive bias for multimodal fusion. Pretrained visual and textual features are projected into compact latent spaces, encoded as angle-parameterized quantum states, processed through intra-modal and paired cross-modal entangling circuits, and measured to produce fused representations for retrieval. Under matched parameter budgets and identical frozen CLIP backbones, QEMFN outperforms classical fusion baselines on COCO-5k and Flickr30k, including multilayer perceptron, tensor fusion, FiLM, cross-attention, compact transformer, and a dequantized paired-topology analogue. An ablation suite isolates the quantum module's contribution from the surrounding classical projections, and quantum-centric analyses report Meyer-Wallach entangling capability, expressibility, gradient variance against barren-plateau bounds, and entropy-performance correlation under controls for training progress alongside an intervention study on the entangling component. QEMFN is executed under shot-based estimation, a noise-modeled fake backend, and a real superconducting device with zero-noise extrapolation. This work does not claim quantum computational advantage; the contribution is the framework together with a controlled empirical and quantum-centric evaluation that positions trainable entanglement as an interpretable, hardware-executable fusion mechanism at scales accessible on contemporary devices.
summary: This paper introduces QEMFN, a hybrid quantum-classical network that uses parameterized quantum entanglement to fuse vision and language embeddings. It demonstrates that this quantum structure improves retrieval performance over classical methods on standard benchmarks. The work provides a detailed, resource-aware evaluation, confirming the framework's utility without claiming quantum advantage.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of multimodal vision-language fusion, proposing to replace classical fusion operators with a structured, trainable quantum entanglement mechanism.
main_result: The proposed QEMFN outperforms classical fusion baselines on image-text retrieval benchmarks (COCO-5k, Flickr30k) under parameter-matched conditions, demonstrating the utility of trainable entanglement as a fusion bias.
method: It employs a hybrid quantum-classical framework where embeddings are encoded into quantum states, processed through parameterized entangling circuits, and measured to yield a fused representation.
model_or_system: The model uses a quantum circuit structure involving visual and textual qubits, connected by trainable single-qubit rotations and paired cross-modal entangling gates. The computation is evaluated across ideal simulation, shot-based estimation, and real superconducting hardware.
key_observables: Image-text retrieval performance (Recall@1, MRR), von Neumann entropy ($S_{norm}$), Meyer-Wallach entangling capability, and gradient variance.
important_parameters: Matched parameter budgets, number of qubits ($n_q=6$), circuit depth ($L=4$), and noise levels ($p$ for depolarizing channel).
main_assumptions: The work explicitly does not claim quantum computational advantage, as the circuit remains classically simulable at the studied scales.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the QEMFN quantum fusion circuit. Tables compare performance across various classical and quantum fusion methods, and Table XIII details hardware performance across different noise models.
paper_structure: The paper introduces QEMFN, details the quantum encoding and entangling evolution, presents ablation studies isolating the quantum module's contribution, analyzes the correlation between entanglement entropy and performance, and concludes with hardware benchmarking.
why_interesting: The rigorous testing of entanglement dynamics (entropy correlation, intervention studies) and the direct comparison of performance across ideal, simulated, and real superconducting hardware provide a detailed resource characterization of quantum machine learning circuits.

figures.caption: Fig. 1: QEMFN quantum fusion circuit with paired cross-modal entanglement. Visual qubits V0–V5 and textual qubits T0–T5 are prepared from projected modality embeddings, followed by trainable single-qubit rotations, intra-modal entangling layers, and paired cross-modal couplings Vi ↔Ti. Final measurements generate the fused representation used for retrieval.
Fig. 2: Correlation between normalized entanglement entropy and Recall@1 across 12 epochs and 10 random seeds. Each point corresponds to one seed- epoch observation.
